current.text: He has a meniscus injury in his knee and is expected to be out for basically the whole season. Yahoo lists him as out with a knee injury.
Portland's backcourt is crowded. Damian Lillard, Ja Morant, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson and Deni Avdija all compete for on-ball minutes, and Sharpe is listed off the bench.
Josh says there is almost no chance he starts.
His value has cratered in the crowded Portland backcourt, and he cannot be drafted as the roster stands.
It is unclear whether his scoring from last season, which came in a high-volume bench role, was empty or whether he can keep that volume.
His jump in steals came from a 71% deflection-to-steal conversion. The speaker calls this luck, so his steals should come back down.
His potential assists converted at only 47.2%. The speaker blames teammates who finish poorly (Camara, Clingan, Avdija) more than luck.
Portland has a new head coach, and minutes and usage are expected to swing from game to game across the rotation.

note: Both sites give him a value of 0 USD (Yahoo rank 218, ESPN rank 331). Projections cover only 27 to 30 games, which fits a meniscus injury that is expected to cost most of the season. Do not spend a draft pick on him, not even the 4 USD he cost in our league last season. Even when healthy he is a bench scorer in a crowded backcourt, and his categories show no strength. Watch for a return timeline and leave him on waivers until then. Two September notes call him a starter and a round-nine flyer, but they do not fit the facts we have. One says he played 19 minutes last season, while the table shows 29.4. The other names Danny Wolf and Mo Wagner as his minutes rivals. Neither mentions the injury, so they were not used.
